AI-Generated (162 words): Whichever kit you get, start each part at a low dose and build up as your gut gets used to it. That goes most for the prebiotic (resistant starch is one too), since your gut bacteria make gas when they ferment it, and for the probiotic, which can bloat you or upset your stomach at first as well.
Bleeding from your gut or fast weight loss can mean something more serious that supplements won't fix, so see a doctor before you start. So can bad pain or a fever, and so can getting dehydrated. If you're pregnant or your immune system is weak, work out what's safe with your doctor instead of putting a stack together yourself, since berberine isn't safe in pregnancy, and probiotics are live bacteria that a weak immune system can't always keep in check. That goes for an IBD flare too, and for cancer (see the glutamine caution above) or another serious illness.

AI-Generated (50 words): That said, some people want a ready-made stack rather than buying every ingredient for it separately. So, if I were to recommend a general "repair and rebuild" approach, it would be a stack that covers three categories:
First, support the Microbiome with a well-tolerated probiotic or probiotic system.

AI-Generated (47 words): Then keep the probiotics well-fed with a good prebiotic, and take butyrate itself or something that helps short-chain fatty acid production, especially the main one, butyrate.
Other nutrients will help support barrier repair, such as glutamine, zinc carnosine, colostrum, mucosal-support herbs, or similar compounds.

AI-Generated (63 words): Ruscio's Leaky Gut Support Kit has a probiotic and two lining products, one of them glutamine, but no prebiotic, so it's more for when leaky gut is your main problem. And Designs for Health GI Revive is only the third category, a powder of gut-lining nutrients and herbs, so you'd still need a probiotic and a prebiotic with it.
r08-p1: AI-Generated (18 words): A stack is a set of supplements you take together, and none of them replaces the phases above.

AI-Generated (104 words): I don't think there's one stack that heals everyone's gut, because guts go wrong for different reasons, and no kit can release a stuck vagus nerve or get your bile flowing. So whatever you take, keep to the order of the phases: get your digestion working mechanically first (Phase 1), then reset your diet and your meal spacing (Phase 2), and only go after bugs and parasites (Phase 3) if you still have symptoms after that. A stack is for the rebuilding in Phase 5, once you're clear of infection and it's time to feed the good bacteria again.
